claims.text: Toughness retention in high-entropy alloys is governed predominantly by grain-boundary stabilization through solute segregation.
A tailored annealing and controlled-cooling treatment can selectively enhance solute segregation at grain boundaries without altering the primary bulk phase.
Enhanced solute segregation stabilizes grain boundaries.
Enhanced solute segregation produces a serrated grain-boundary morphology.
Strain localization along phase or grain boundaries can lead to crack initiation in multi-principal-element alloys.
Stabilized, serrated grain boundaries reduce local strain concentrations.
Stabilized, serrated grain boundaries facilitate crack deflection.
Grain-boundary stabilization through solute segregation facilitates crack bridging.
Crack deflection and bridging can contribute to toughening by shielding crack tips or mitigating strain localization.
Reduced strain localization and enhanced crack deflection suppress intergranular crack initiation and propagation.
Tailored heat-treated specimens will have higher fracture toughness than conventionally processed specimens.
Tailored heat-treated specimens will show delayed crack initiation relative to conventionally processed specimens.
Tailored heat-treated specimens will have greater ductility than conventionally processed specimens.
Tailored heat-treated specimens will exhibit more serrated and stable grain boundaries than the baseline.
The more serrated and stable grain-boundary morphology will correlate with improved crack deflection.
The proposed behavior applies to single-phase or controlled-multiphase high-entropy alloys when the bulk microstructure is maintained.
The proposed behavior applies below processing temperatures that cause extensive recrystallization or phase transformation.
Phase constitution and processing-induced microstructural evolution can affect the mechanical properties of compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys.
The relative contribution of grain-boundary stabilization to toughness may vary with alloy composition and processing parameters.
